market: Every category is converging on agents and MCP: data vendors, signal tools, engagement suites, CRMs, and AI-native startups all shipped agent features in the last 12 months.

Pricing is moving from seats to credits to outcomes: HubSpot $1/recommended lead, Salesforce 400 Flex Credits per lead worked, Rox Agent Actions, seatless Clay and Monaco, and ZoomInfo moving seats to pre-bought consumption. Sales Navigator is the pure-seat outlier.
LLMs are becoming the workspace: competitors pipe data into Claude and ChatGPT through MCP. No public Sales Navigator MCP found (unverified).
Platforms are buying the signal layer: Zoom bought Common Room, Salesloft merged with Clari, ZoomInfo bought DoubleO.ai.
LinkedIn data stays scarce and legally defended (ProAPIs judgment 2026-09-16). Rivals route around it with third-party data, and CRM agents bundle ZoomInfo and Apollo, not LinkedIn.
threats: CRM agents (Salesforce Hunter, HubSpot Prospecting Agent) own prospecting with non-LinkedIn data
Absent from Claude and ChatGPT, where rivals now meet sellers
Signal agents (UserGems, Unify, Common Room) automate SN's job-change and warm-path use cases
Seatless and outcome pricing undercuts $119.99 seats
Clay as the GTM-engineer data hub replacing SN data seats
openings: First-party profile and relationship data, legally defended
Ship an SN agent/MCP and an agent-consumption tier (per lead or per insight)
Turn CRM integrations (Advanced Plus) into agent data feeds, not view-only cards
Microsoft Copilot, Teams, and Dynamics distribution
Mid-market opening from ZoomInfo weakness (NRR 89%, downmarket ACV down 12%)
moves: Lead with 'agents are only as good as their people data': LinkedIn first-party, consented, fresh
Position SN as the relationship layer every agent needs (warm paths, TeamLink) rather than another contact DB
Offer usage-based access for agents alongside seats to meet credit and outcome buyers
